edited_rows.rationale: Second-person address to God opens the row at web:Ps.76.4 (“Glorious are you, and excellent…”) immediately after the Selah closing the prior unit (web:Ps.76.3 = oshb:Ps.76.4, “סֶֽלָה”), and the same address sustains through the vocative at web:Ps.76.6, “At your rebuke, God of Jacob…” (oshb:Ps.76.7 “אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב”), and the fear-vocabulary of web:Ps.76.7-8 (“You, even you, are to be feared… You pronounced judgment from heaven…”). The psalm's second Selah, web:Ps.76.9 (oshb:Ps.76.10 “לְהוֹשִׁ֖יעַ כָּל עַנְוֵי אֶ֣רֶץ סֶֽלָה”), sits inside the row rather than closing it: the God-directed address continues past it, without a person change, through the row's own close at web:Ps.76.10, “Surely the wrath of man praises you. The survivors of your wrath are restrained.” The closing verb's own suffix, “תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ” (oshb:Ps.76.11, final kaf + dagesh + qamats), is second-person-masculine-singular, 'it praises you', so the address opened at web:Ps.76.4 runs to this row's own close without an addressee change. The seam falls right after it: web:Ps.76.11 (oshb:Ps.76.12) opens the plural imperative summons, “Make vows to Yahweh your God…”, addressed to the worshiping congregation rather than to God -- the addressee shift that closes this row.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending the row through web:Ps.76.11 (oshb:Ps.76.12) was rejected: its plural imperative, “Make vows to Yahweh your God, and fulfill them!”, addresses the worshiping congregation rather than God, so folding it into this row would erase the addressee change the seam is meant to mark; this row's own close instead sits one verse earlier, at web:Ps.76.10 (oshb:Ps.76.11), whose own verb, “תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ”, still carries the second-person address to God that opened the row at web:Ps.76.4.
